//: CaseBook PRODUCTION configuration template. Copy to the deployed site as appsettings.Production.json and fill its placeholder tokens (the UPPER_CASE names wrapped in double underscores). Install-CaseBook.ps1 does this substitution for you. Never commit the filled-in file - it names AD groups and hosts. Secrets are NOT stored here (integrated auth to SQL; signing key on disk/HSM).

Auth.//: Production MUST be Windows; the app refuses to start otherwise (F-02).

ConnectionStrings.//: Windows integrated auth - no credentials. Encrypt in transit. Set TrustServerCertificate=False once SQL Server presents a CA-signed certificate. (MARS/MultipleActiveResultSets is no longer needed: since H-08 the app uses a DbContext factory with a short-lived context per operation, so there are no overlapping readers on one connection - validated on SQL Server 2022.)

EvidenceStore.//: Absolute paths OUTSIDE the web root, on an ACL-restricted, backed-up, EDR-monitored volume.

Encryption.//: PROD-57: evidence and reports encrypted at rest. The key is protected by CertificateThumbprint if set, else by the integrity certificate (chain key's, else signing) or the CyberArk chain key. Nothing is encrypted until a backup exists: RecoveryCertificates (.cer files, public part only; their private keys offline) or shares from casebook-keytool split. Losing the key loses the encrypted files: read OPERATIONS.md section 2 (Evidence key) first.

ReportBranding.//: H-07: the deployment report logo (one image for the whole install) lives on the ACL'd data volume, NOT under the web root, so the site can stay read-only. Set in-app under Administration -> Settings -> Reporting.

ReportTemplates.//: PROD-47: customer-designed Word report templates (one per report profile), uploaded under Administration -> Reports.

Config.//: CAP-16: a folder of public keys (PEM) whose configuration bundles import here without a typed key id, besides this server's own; for example the test server's, exported from its Integrity page. Blank = none. Read at startup; a file that isn't an RSA key stops it.

Integrity.//: Provision the signing key OUT OF BAND (do not let the app generate it in prod) - see OPERATIONS.md section 2.

SigningKey.//: F-23: where the seal signing key comes from. File (the PEM at SigningKeyPath), CertificateStore (CertificateThumbprint in LocalMachine\My; the app account needs read on its private key) or CyberArk (Secret = an @cyberark:Safe=...;Object=... reference to the PEM). Retired public keys for rotation go in RetiredPublicKeysPath (blank = a 'retired' folder beside SigningKeyPath). See OPERATIONS.md section 2.

ChainKey.//: F-25: hash the audit chain with a secret key (HMAC-SHA256) so database access alone can't rewrite recent history. OFF by default, and one-way in practice: keyed entries can only be checked while their key is held, so back the key up first. Source CyberArk (Secret = an @cyberark: reference to 32 random bytes, base64; earlier keys in RetiredSecrets) or Certificate (CertificateThumbprint; the key is generated once and kept encrypted at WrappedKeyPath, earlier ones in RetiredWrappedKeysPath). See OPERATIONS.md section 2.

SealCopies.//: F-27: optional extra copies of each seal, each off while blank. EmailTo: addresses for a seal digest (a mailbox under retention; needs email on in-app). TimestampAuthorityUrl: an INTERNAL RFC 3161 timestamp authority (only private addresses are accepted); tokens are saved beside each seal in ExportPath. Seals also go to the SIEM as event 5004 whenever a SIEM transport is on. See OPERATIONS.md section 2.

Security.//: F-15: idle-session timeout. After this many minutes with no keyboard/mouse activity the working circuit is torn down and the screen is locked behind a neutral page, requiring the user to resume. This COMPLEMENTS the OS/AD workstation screen-lock (which enforces credential re-entry) - it does not replace it; keep it aligned with your screen-lock GPO. 0 disables the app-level timeout. Administered in-app under Administration -> Settings -> Security; this is the fallback default.

Reporting.//: E-15: when true, a report must be approved by someone other than the analyst who generated it (two-person / maker-checker control). The approver + timestamp is recorded either way. Administered in-app under Administration -> Settings -> Reporting; this is the fallback default.

DataProtection.//: Persist the antiforgery/circuit keyring so sessions survive app-pool recycles. Absolute, ACL-restricted folder; keys are encrypted at rest with DPAPI (machine scope).

Secrets.//: F-19: optional CyberArk CCP secret retrieval (setup: INSTALL.md section 6.1; full reference: OPERATIONS.md section 6). Leave Enabled=false to keep secrets literal. When Enabled, write a secret as a reference like '@cyberark:Safe=SIEM;Object=CaseBook-Webhook-Token' (e.g. as Siem:Webhook:Token) instead of a literal. No CCP password is stored: your CyberArk admin decides how the AppID authenticates (client certificate, Allowed-Machines source IP/hostname, and/or OS user). The ONLY auth method that needs a value here is a client certificate; source-IP and OS-user auth need no CaseBook config (they use this host and the app-pool identity).

CyberArk.//BaseUrl: The CyberArk CCP (AIMWebService) URL, e.g. https://ccp.corp.example/AIMWebService. Must be HTTPS.
CyberArk.//AppId: The Application ID your CyberArk admin provisioned for CaseBook.
CyberArk.//ClientCertificateThumbprint: Set ONLY if the AppID requires a client cert; the cert must be in LocalMachine\My with the app-pool identity granted read on its private key. Blank = rely on Allowed-Machines / OS-user auth.

Downloads.//: F-13: per-user token bucket on the evidence/report/export download endpoints. TokenLimit is the burst; TokensPerPeriod refill over PeriodSeconds sets the sustained rate. Over budget => immediate 429 + a SIEM event (5306). Server-side security config; restart to change.

Siem.//: F-18: outbound security-event stream to SIEM. Transports (webhook JSON, syslog CEF) fan out from a bounded queue. Endpoints/secret stay in server-side config (not the in-app editable settings); status is shown read-only in Admin. Both transports disabled by default.

Webhook.//: JSON POST to the SIEM HTTP Collector. AuthHeader/AuthScheme match the collector (Authorization: Bearer, or x-api-key). Token may be a literal or, with Secrets:CyberArk enabled (F-19), a reference like '@cyberark:Safe=SIEM;Object=CaseBook-Webhook-Token' fetched from CyberArk CCP at runtime, or a @protected: value. CAP-40: leave Token blank to enter it in Administration (Integrations, SIEM webhook token, encrypted with Data Protection); set here, it wins. A token that won't resolve or decrypt stops the send rather than sending without it.

Syslog.//: CEF over syslog to an SIEM Broker VM / syslog collector. Protocol Udp (fire-and-forget), Tcp or Tls (CAP-33: RFC 5425, usually port 6514; the collector certificate must be trusted and issued to Host; optional ServerCertificateThumbprint pin and ClientCertificateThumbprint in LocalMachine\My). Facility 16 = local0.

EventLog.//: Windows Event Log (Windows hosts only). Register the source once, as an administrator, before enabling: New-EventLog -LogName Application -Source CaseBook.

Chat.//: PROD-02: outbound team-chat notification channel (Slack/Teams incoming webhook), a broadcast alongside email. The webhook URL is the channel credential, so it stays in server-side config (not the in-app catalog) and shows read-only in Admin -> Server configuration. Which notification types post here is chosen in-app under Notifications:Chat. Disabled by default; https-only egress.

Webhook.//: WebhookUrl is the Slack Incoming Webhook URL or a Teams channel connector/workflow URL. It may be a literal or, with Secrets:CyberArk enabled (F-19), a reference like '@cyberark:Safe=SOC;Object=CaseBook-Chat-Webhook', or a @protected: value. CAP-40: leave WebhookUrl blank to enter it in Administration (Settings, Notifications, Team chat webhook, encrypted with Data Protection); set here, it wins. Format: Slack (mrkdwn text) or Teams (MessageCard).

Updates.//: PROD-49: the update check. CheckEnabled and CheckIntervalHours are admin-editable (Administration -> Updates); Repository and Proxy stay server-side. One anonymous GET to api.github.com; nothing about the installation is sent. Off by default.

Agenda.//: E-39: signing secret for the per-user agenda calendar (ICS) subscription feed (/agenda/feed.ics?token=...). Server-side only (a bearer secret, like the seal signing key) - NOT admin-editable. Blank = the subscribable feed is disabled (the authenticated one-shot download /agenda/agenda.ics still works). Set a long random value in appsettings.Production.json to enable Outlook subscriptions; rotating it invalidates every issued feed URL.

BackupStatus.//: H-04: JSON status file the out-of-band SQL backup + restore-verification jobs write (OPERATIONS.md section 1.3.1).

Email.//: IntegrityAlertDistribution (F-16): SysAdmin/SecOps recipients alerted if the audit hash-chain fails verification (a possible tamper event). A critical SIEM/log event (EventId 5001) is emitted regardless; wire it to a SIEM detection rule. Editable in-app under Administration -> Settings -> Notifications.
Email.//EnableSsl: Encrypt the SMTP connection (STARTTLS). Server-side only; default true. Set false only for a relay that terminates TLS itself (e.g. a trusted localhost submission agent).
Email.//SmtpSignIn: CAP-05: how CaseBook signs in to the relay. Usually left blank here and set in-app (Administration -> Settings -> Notifications -> Email sign-in), where the password is encrypted with Data Protection. Set here, it wins over the form: SmtpUsername with SmtpPassword (a @protected: value from deploy\keytool\casebook-keytool protect-secret, an @cyberark: reference, or a plain-text literal, which Diagnostics warns of), OR SmtpUseDefaultCredentials=true to sign in as the app-pool account (on-premises Exchange; no password). Not both. SmtpTimeoutSeconds: 5 to 300. See OPERATIONS.md section 6.

RoleMapping.//: Map REAL Active Directory security-group names to application roles. These seed the DB role directory on first run (thereafter manage in-app under Administration -> Roles).
